answer: Treat each active identity as a congestible resource and levy a Pigouvian toll: every agent-seat pays a per-epoch fee equal to the marginal load it imposes on shared verification bandwidth, a fee that climbs convexly with total seat count. One honest agent ties up at the jetty for a flat base; a swarm crowding the same narrow ridge of audit capacity drives the toll up per extra clone, the 500th seat owes ~500x base, so at 2 POA that swarm pays ~250,000 POA versus 2 once. The nectar a sybil hoped to skim is taxed away, internalizing the externality so minting identities stops paying.
